articleTitle: A Hybrid Coaxial Magnetic Gear Using Flux-Focusing Halbach Permanent Magnet Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: The interest in developing magnetic gears (MGs) has been considerably increased in recent years due to the numerous advantages such as high torque density, low maintenance and overload protection. In this paper, a new MG that integrates flux-focusing and Halbach configurations is proposed. The special design of the radially magnetized permanent magnets (PMs) at both edges of the inner rotor improves the magnetic field distribution and enables the proposed MG to be designed with a high torque density. Parameter sweep analysis is used to maximize the torque density of the proposed flux-focusing Halbach coaxial MG (FFH-CMG), and reduce the volume of PM material used in the design. Finally, the electromagnetic performance of the proposed FFH-CMG is investigated using both 2D and 3D finite element analysis (FEA). The results show that the proposed FFH-CMG can achieve the largest torque density when compared with its counterparts and maintain a low torque ripple.

articleTitle: Three-Phase AC/DC Converter fed Two Parallel Interleaved DC-DC Converters for Fast Charging Applications with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel grid-interactive, off-board, three-phase EV charger and its control strategy are presented with the potential to achieve desired power factor. In the proposed configuration, the dual-stage (AC-DC and DC-DC) integrated charger is composed of a three-phase AC/DC converter and the two-phase parallel interleaved DC-DC converter sharing the same dc-link. The AC-DC converter interface between input mains and the dc-link. The parallel interleaved DC-DC converter is connected between the dc-link and the EV battery.The entire system is designed for a 3-ϕ, 10 kW rating with a broad range DC output voltage of 200–400V for EV batteries and 400V rms phase–to–phase, 50 Hz input supply. The designed converter is capability to provide enhanced low input and output current ripple with low input total current harmonics (THD), robust regulation of DC-link voltage, desired power factor and less ripple output voltage. The outcomes of the EV charger are anticipated by the MATLAB/ SIMULINK results which verify theoretical analysis. The near UPF of the system is improved by the suggested charger's compliance with the IEC 61000-3-2 standard, which also increases system reliability and efficiency. Based on the results, the system appears to be a viable fast charging solution for EVs, as it reaches 97.8% efficiency with 0.9997 PF and 2.54% THD at the source.

articleTitle: Application of Partical Swarm Optimization Algorithm On Nonlinear PI Controllers for Stable Operation of DFIG Based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents an optimally tuned Nonlinear Proportional Integral (NPI) controllers design for the inner and outer loops of the control algorithm for Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) based Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG). There are many WECS control techniques like direct torque control and direct active and reactive power control which is used in this paper using NPI control, of the rotor side converter, where the actuating signal equals to the summation of proportional and integral of nonlinear functions of the error signal. A Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to get the optimal integral and proportional gains under presence of the perturbation and during transition during wind speed change. However, Integral Square Error (ISE) and Integral Time Square Error (ITSE) performance indices, are considered to solve the nonlinear and non-differential problem due the uncertainty of the generated power from the Wind Turbine (WT). To validate the proposed approach, Matlab Simulink environment is used.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements in Solid State Transformer-based EV Fast Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Growing deployments of ultra fast charging stations (XFCS) are putting a stress on the existing line-frequency transformer (LFT)-based medium voltage (MV) grid due to the high charging demands of exponentially growing electric vehicles (EV). The conventional LFT occupies a large space in the XFCS installation which introduces challenges in facilitating the XFCS infrastructure. As a result, solid-state transformer (SST)-based XFCS are being developed which can be directly connected to the MV grid and several advantages over LFT-based systems such as compactness, intelligence and availability of the DC link to connect renewable energy sources and storage system can be realized. As such, a detailed analysis of current developments in SST-based XFCS is presented and compared with one another in this paper. The challenges associated with the configurations are examined and direction for future research is identified.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Electric Motors by a Novel Convolutional-based Neural Network and STFT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for fault detection in electric motors based on Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and a regulated convolutional-based neural network. In this method, STFT is applied over the raw signal measured from the motor to generate a 2D matrix as an input to a classification model. The classification model constitutes a regulated network combining Convolutional Long Short Term Memory (ConvLSTM) andConvolutional Neural Network (CNN) which is developed to be fit for the low-size 2D STFT matrices. The proposed method is evaluated over, a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) with healthy and three levels of Inter-Turn Short Circuit (ITSC) fault conditions. The model is also tested under the influence of measurement noise. The model has shown a good performance for all these conditions.

articleTitle: Online Winding Reconfiguration of a Multiphase Stator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: A multiphase machine control implementing vector space decomposition or harmonic plane decomposition for modeling purposes can reconfigure the stator's current distribution to generate magnetomotive force waves with different pole pair numbers simultaneously. The pole pair numbers are an integer multiple of the pole pairs generated by the physical winding configuration. This property can be used for reconfiguring the pole-pair number in real time or increasing the system's torque density. This paper studies the modeling and the impact of symmetrical and asymmetrical winding configurations on the pole-pair number reconfiguration. Furthermore, pole number transition is experimentally verified on a proposed winding configuration.

articleTitle: Thirteen-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Converters and 30-Pulse Converter Transformer Based High-Power Voltage Source Converters for Large-Scale Integration of Battery Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid high-power voltage source converter (VSC) based on thirteen-level cascaded H-bridge (CHB) converters and 30-pulse high voltage converter transformer configuration for large-scale integration of battery energy storage (BES). VSC voltage harmonics mitigation is realized with the combined effect of the multi-pulse converter and fundamental switched selective harmonics elimination (SHE) technique employed in CHB converters. A low THD is obtained for VSC output voltage and grid currents. Multiple CHB along with high voltage transformers is used in VSC to increase its power and energy capacity and this allows to BES plant to collect and deliver energy at 400kV voltage level to the grid. A 1000MW and 6000MWh BES plant is modeled in MATLAB-Simulink to demonstrate its steady state, harmonics, and dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Control Strategies For Optimal Power Flow Management and Enhanced Cycle Life Of Battery-Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (HESS) utilises various combinations of electrochemical and electrostatic potential and couples two or more energy storage architectures to achieve a broader range of characteristics in terms of power density, energy density and lifetime. In this paper, passive and active topology configurations of HESS and their control strategies are tested and discussed with results as well as possible future work. A reduced stress on the primary energy storage battery pack is achieved by Passive HESS Topology which increases the cycle life and reduces capacity fading.

articleTitle: A Novel Islanding Detection Method Based on a Hybrid Algorithm in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new fast and reliable technique for detecting islanding in DC power systems. This approach involves injecting a periodic disturbance into the DC network at specific intervals. Detectors at each microgrid DC link monitor the system parameters. A real-time signal processing analyzer makes the decision to trip circuit breakers in the event of islanding conditions. The proposed technique is easy to implement and does not require a separate communication infrastructure. Simulation results confirm that the method meets the IEEE 1547 Standard, and demonstrates the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A High Gain Expandable DC-DC Converter with PSO-based MPPT Tracking for Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: To match up the voltage requirement at the utility or transmission side, a high-gain DC-DC converter is often required to elevate the low output voltage of solar PV. Also, to harness the peak power from the solar panel, many algorithms have been given but the conventional algorithm is only suitable for the single peak PV characteristics. In partial shading conditions, multi-peak PV characteristics are observed where a heuristic approach-based algorithm is needed to track the global peak power from PV characteristics. So, in this paper, a high-gain expandable DC-DC converter is proposed that incorporates a particle swarm optimization (PSO) based MPPT tracking algorithm for solar PV applications. The configuration of the proposed high gain converter is comprised of an L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n-2</inf> network and it can be expanded up to n-cells where each cell consists of one inductor, two capacitors, and one diode. To analyze the performance of the converter, n=3 i.e., the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> network-based converter has been chosen. The PSO-based MPPT algorithm has been applied to track the global peak power under partial shading conditions in MATLAB. Also, a 300 W scaled-down laboratory prototype is developed and tested under steady-state and dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: A Review of Fault-Tolerant Control Methods for Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper is a comprehensive survey of existing fault-tolerant control methods for the cascaded H-bridge inverter (CHBI) with faulty cells. These methods are widely proposed in the literature to rebalance the CHBI output line-to-line voltages even if its line-to-neutral voltages remain unbalanced due to the failed cells. However, the details of their performances are dispersed across the literature. Hence, the paper discusses a comparative analysis of the most common fault-tolerant control techniques. First, these control approaches are classified according to their operational principle, key features, and limitations. Then, a detailed description of each method is discussed, where analytical expressions of their respective algorithm and implementation scheme are provided. For comparison purposes, extensive simulation results at various operating points are provided for a three-phase, seven-level CHBI topology supplying an induction motor. The comparison performance between the investigated methods is performed based on the magnitude of the common-mode voltage, the maximum achievable balanced line-to-line voltage, the current unbalanced ratio, as well as their total harmonic distortion values at various operating points.

articleTitle: Capacitor Voltages Balancing Method for Flying Capacitor Multilevel Converters Based on Overall Priority Index
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: In this paper, a generalized method for voltage balancing is proposed that can be applied to all multilevel converters that utilize flying capacitors. The proposed method determines a priority index (PI) based on the charging and discharging status of flying capacitors in different redundant switching states. Using the overall priority index (OPI), which represents the sum of PIs in a phase, the proper switching state is selected that will result in the appropriate voltage balancing of flying capacitors. To calculate the OPI, the proposed method employs phase current direction and capacitor voltage deviation, resulting in less hardware and software complexity than methods that use cost functions. This paper presents a systematic method for calculating the OPI. In addition, a simplified OPI calculation method is presented for the classic flying capacitor multicell (FCM) topologies. For a five-level FCM converter, the method is illustrated. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in regulating flying capacitor voltages. Furthermore, the results show a good dynamic response when the operating point changes. Both capacitor voltage ripples and switching frequencies are considered in the comparison. In a laboratory setup, the proposed method is demonstrated to be practicable.

articleTitle: Efficiency Improvement of Induction Machine Powertrain by High Switching Frequency and Wide Bandgap Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: It was investigated how the efficiency of a high-speed induction machine and the related powertrain can be improved by using high switching frequencies. These were enabled by use of wideband gap semiconductors. A model of an induction machine, sensitive to voltage harmonics, was derived and implemented in order to determine the efficiency of the powertrain as a function of the inverter switching frequency. The powertrain, mainly including the inverter and the motor, was simulated for different load situations and power classes. The optimum switching frequency resulting in the best overall system efficiency, was determined for different Vertical GaN and SiC based inverter implementations.

articleTitle: EMI investigation of a Bridgeless-PFC LED Driver with Direct Power Transfer Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues pertaining to an isolated bridgeless single-stage, light-emitting diode (LED) driver. The front-end of the converter consists of a Power factor correction (PFC) circuit and a soft-switching technique to ensure a close to unity power factor. In addition, a complementary circuit is added to directly transfer power from the primary circuit to the load using a couple-inductor to reduce the stress on the MOSFETs switches while guaranteeing maximum power throughput. Due to the switching nature of this topology with high di/dt and dv/dt, a significant EMI noise, in both common and differential modes, is generated in the primary circuit, which can find its way back to the utility grid. Thus, compliance with applicable Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) standards is required. Further details relevant to the circuit CM and DM noise issues will be discussed. An EMI filter design will be illustrated and results for the conducted EMI emission will be provided.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Self-Compensated Coil Geometries for Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Self-resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) system can achieve high reliability due to the elimination of physical compensation capacitors. Planar coils that have parasitic capacitance between adjacent layers are ideal candidates for self-resonant WPT systems, and the coil geometry has a significant influence on the performance of WPT system. This paper studies and compares three typical coil geometries, namely circular, square, and hexagonal coils. The mutual inductance, coupling coefficient, magnetic field of coils, ac resistance, output power, and efficiency have been calculated and compared using finite element method. Simulation results show that hexagonal planar coil can transfer the largest power and has the highest efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Multi-Modulation Single-Carrier PWM Methods for Motor Drive Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Due to their numerous benefits, multi-modulation single-carrier pulse width modulation (MSC-PWM) approaches are becoming more prevalent in multilevel converter topology control systems. Compared to traditional multi-carrier PWM techniques, MSC-PWM methods present more straightforward real-time implementation, while achieving acceptable harmonic performances. However, their application remains limited to grid integration of photovoltaic converter systems, and no literature examines their suitability and effectiveness in multilevel converters supplying electrical machines. This paper uses the traditional and modified MSC-PWM methods to discuss the design and implementation of vector control for an induction motor fed by a multilevel cascaded H-bridge inverter. First, the vector control scheme is briefly introduced, and then each MSC-PWM method’s implementation scheme is thoroughly described. Then, the effectiveness of the investigated MSC-PWM methods is evaluated through steady-state and dynamic computer simulation results. Finally, a performance comparison of different PWM methods is conducted based on the spectra and THDs of the motor voltage, current, and electromagnetic torque. According to the comparison study, the modified MSC-PWM technique is superior to the conventional MSC-PWM method in reducing the motor voltage THD by up to 30%, motor current THD by up to 40%, and subsequently reducing the torque ripple in the motor air gap.

articleTitle: Irreversible demagnetization risk of rotor-surface-mounted permanent magnets at rated and short-circuit modes in two-pole multi-megawatt machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: The flux density distribution of a rotor-surface-magnet two-pole 4 MW permanent-magnet synchronous machine with a solid rotor core is studied in three different operating modes: rated operation, two- and three-phase short circuits. Demagnetizing field strength by the armature reaction at the rated operation of multimegawatt two-pole machines can be significant, and it should be ensured that coercivity in the magnets is not decreased due to irreversible demagnetization. Significant demagnetization field can take place during the transient of two- or three-phase short circuit. In this work, the capability of the magnets to withstand short-circuits in multi-megawatt two-pole machines regarding the risk of irreversible demagnetization is investigated. To evaluate the role of the solid rotor core in short-circuit tolerance of the machine, short-circuit tests were performed in transient 2D Finite Element Method (FEM) model and the results were compared with similar tests when the rotor yoke is replaced with a traditional lamination stack.

articleTitle: Fast Electromagnetic and Thermal Design Space Analysis for PMSM Propeller Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: In this paper a fast procedure for the design of interior rotor and outer rotor permanent magnet synchronous machines is presented. It is used for an initial investigation of the design space at an early development stage for aircraft application. It is extended with a lumped parameter thermal network (LPTN) model to enable equally fast feedback on thermal stability. The high potential of this tool is demonstrated with the fast investigation of design choices on other design aspects in multiple engineering disciplines even at an early design stage. It is used to evaluate the use of outer/inner rotor, different coolants and cooling structures.

articleTitle: An Electric Vehicle Circuit for Powering Independent Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper designs and simulates a vehicle-to-load system using a Nissan Leaf electric car at the solar house of Concordia University, Montréal, Canada. This research facility is built to investigate numerous renewable energy systems to achieve net-zero energy for a typical detached single-family dwelling in Québec. This building, known as Future Buildings Laboratory (FBL), has integrated renewable energy sources such as solar, solar-thermal, and wind, allowing the opportunity to test different power management scenarios. The vehicle-to-load system is designed and simulated in MATLAB software considering the house's rated load and the Nissan Leaf battery's rating. The design reflects the actual characteristics of the load, battery, and power electronic elements and their interaction.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Sliding Mode Controller for Direct Torque Control of Four-Wheel Drive Electrical Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: To improve vehicle handling characteristics of Electric Vehicles (EV), recent system control studies make it possible to operate driving wheel torques separately have been carried out. In this paper a fuzzy sliding-mode controller based on the hybridization between fuzzy logic and sliding mode control has been applied for the Direct Torque Control (DTC) of 4 Wheel Drive Electric Vehicle (4WDEV). Using MATLAB Simulink environment, a comparison of simulation results, application of the FSMC and the Sliding Mode Control (SMC), proved that the application of the FSMC technique presents a better alleviation of the chattering phenomenon and increases trajectory tracking performance.

articleTitle: A Fast Active Cell Balancing Strategy for Lithium-ion Battery Packs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Development of reliable and efficient battery management systems (BMS) is determinant in the path of vehicles towards electrification. In this work, we speed up the cell balancing process of a Li-ion battery pack by introducing a novel state-of-charge (SOC) balancing strategy. The strategy takes advantage of the existing 12 volts battery in electric and hybrid vehicles as an auxiliary dc bus assisting with the SOC balancing process for the Li-ion battery pack. The proposed method is capable of conveying energy for up to five adjacent cells for SOC balancing. The simulation results on a string of 8 series cells confirm the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: A Study of High-Efficiency/High-Density Phase Shift Full Bridge Converter with Low Profile Two-Transformer Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Interest in environmental protection, particularly low-carbon policies, is rapidly increasing. Along with the development of various technologies and functions in the automobile industry, the electric vehicle market is also experiencing significant growth. One area of active research in electric vehicles is the development of high-efficiency and high-density Low DC-DC Converters(LDC), which convert the high voltage of the main battery into a low voltage of 8-16V. This paper focuses on the study of an LDC based on a Phase Shift Full Bridge (PSFB) Converter with a low height Two-Transformer structure, with the goal of achieving high efficiency and density of the LDC.

articleTitle: Development of IEMI Generator for High Voltage EV Component EMC Test
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Through Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI) generator design, a simulator was developed for the purpose of studying the effects of damage in the intentional EM disturbance environment test of unmanned aerial vehicles, ships, railroads, and electric vehicles & autonomous vehicles. The IEMI generator used Marx topology as a multi-stage pulse forming device. It was manufactured to make it compact, lightweight, and capable of control using SiC MOSFET devices instead of the spark gap, which is a mechanical component. Using IEMI generator, it is possible to secure countermeasure technologies such as electromagnetic wave robust design technology such as verifying conducted immunity of electric vehicles and future autonomous vehicle component and designing EMI filters.

articleTitle: LQ Zero-Sum Differential Games for Stochastic Delay Systems and Application to Stability Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider linear-quadratic zero-sum differential games for a class of stochastic systems with state delay and their application to the stability control problem of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). First, we define a stabilization problem via a memoryless state feedback strategy and then solve the problem of minimizing the upper bound of the cost function using guaranteed cost control theory. Moreover, a saddle point equilibrium condition is established against external disturbance input. For this problem, the necessary conditions for the sub-optimality are established via stochastic cross-coupled matrix equations (SCCMEs) using the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker condition. Second, a practical example based on the stability control problem for the PMSM is presented to demonstrate the usefulness and effectiveness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy is effective even in the presence of stochastic noise, deterministic disturbance, and model uncertainties.

articleTitle: Optimization of Diesel Generator Usage for Multi-Source Nano-Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Multi-source electrical systems rely on performing energy management to have a minimal operational cost while satisfying the energy demand. In this paper, an existing hybrid nano-grid composed of PV panels, a diesel generator, and batteries is used for the investigation purpose. The behavior of the actual electrical system is studied through its equivalent model developed in MATLAB/Simulink®. Recently, we noticed space for improvement in the control settings of the multi-source system. To further confirm the impact of these input set points on the usage of the diesel engine, a sensitivity analysis is also performed. An optimization based on a genetic algorithm demonstrates that changing these control set points through the different periods of the year could improve diesel engine usage and help to penetrate more renewable energy from PV modules.

articleTitle: Novel Two-Stage AC-DC Power Converter with Partial Single-Stage Power Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: AC-DC power conversion is typically implemented with two converter stages: an AC-DC boost converter stage followed by a zero-voltage switching (ZVS) pulse-width modulated (PWM) full-bridge converter stage. An active auxiliary circuit is often used to reduce switching losses in the first-stage converter. The use of such a circuit to transfer a portion of the input power directly to the output of a two-stage AC-DC converter is investigated in the paper. Such direct power transfer (DPT) allows a portion of the power from the input to be processed only once, instead of twice, thus reducing the losses and the current stresses of the second-stage DC-DC converter. In this paper, the basic operating principles of the converter are explained, the features of the first-stage AC-DC boost converter are stated, and a set of guidelines for the design of the converter are given. The feasibility of the proposed converter is confirmed with experimental results.

articleTitle: Charging system for electric vehicles in off-grid isolated areas without electrical network using PV with WiFi telemetry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Due to the significant advantages of electric vehicles that surpass conventional vehicles in terms of high efficiency and environmental friendliness, the production and use of electric vehicles (EVs) is rapidly advancing. The integration of renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic energy (PV) and energy storage system plays an important role for enclave areas where the power grid does not arrive. For example, in the case of a rural area where there is no electricity network and a user of an EV might want to recharge his car with the use of PV energy. However, given the fluctuation of the power production generated by PV, it is important to include the system monitoring factor to keep track at each moment of how much energy is produced. This paper presents a study of a dimensioning of an autonomous charging station for electric vehicles powered by PV energy with a telemetry system that can be used on isolated off-grid areas without electrical network. For the data acquisition part of the project, a LabVIEW program was developed using WiFi technology to receive all the data coming from the energy sources. The study shows that it would be possible to recharge an EV with a photovoltaic energy system and to benefit of the telemetry system implemented.

articleTitle: Single Phase AC Source Motor Drive With Small DC-Link Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents single-phase AC source motor drive method for home appliance system with a small DC-link capacitor. Typically, reducing the physical size of a DC-link capacitor is valuable because small DC-link capacitor-based motor drives are commercially available, and they can supply power with high-power densities. At the AC–DC converter part, the interleaving control method is commonly used, because this method can reduce the root mean square current of a DC-link capacitor, so we can use small size capacitor. But, At the inverter part, it is difficult to reduce capacitor size using conventional motor control method. Therefore, new current control method for the AC source motor drive is proposed in this paper. The proposed current control method yields the desired regulation performance even with the small DC-link capacitor. The control method is based on modifying the reference motor current of d and q-axis PI controller. Its inverter current waveform has an AC source form. Simulation and experimental results show the performance of the proposed current control method.

articleTitle: A Novel Switched Capacitor DC-AC Converter with Hysteresis Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Switched Capacitor Converter (SCCs) for DC-AC conversion is an area of keen interest owing to their benefits and application in many diverse fields related to renewable energy technology. SC-based inverters have advantages such as step-up voltage capability, operating without output side filters, compact design and higher power density. This paper proposes a novel SC-based DC-AC converter with a unique control architecture to achieve AC power at the output. The control architecture utilizes a hysteresis control to track the capacitor voltages to reference and achieve a step-up gain in the output voltage. The proposed converter enables an inherent output voltage ripple reduction by nearly interleaving the charging-discharging phases of the capacitors. Thus, the total harmonic distortion (THD) on the load current is much less.It also eliminates the use of output side magnetic filtering elements and hence removes the drawbacks associated with it. The paper discusses the topology, the control architecture and the challenges involved in optimizing various parameters for the desired operation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control of a Voltage Source Converter Based on the Third-Order Nonlinear Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive controller which provides reactive power compensation and dc voltage tracking for a three-phase Voltage Source Converter (VSC) connected to a power grid system. The novelty of the method lies in the derivation of the adaptive control input and parameter update laws using a bilinear model of the VSC with uncertainties. The suggested approach ensures asymptotic state tracking for the dc voltage and reactive current of the closed-loop system. Simulation and experimental hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) results confirm the controller’s excellent performance.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of VIENNA Circuit Employed Single-Phase Single-Stage Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents modeling and control of a VIENNA circuit employed in a single phase single-stage solar photovoltaic system (SPSSPVS). The topology for the proposed system consists of a half bridge voltage source converter (HBVSC), VIENNA circuit with unidirectional controlled switch and noise absorption (L-RC) filter. The proposed topology of the SPSSPVS offers to minimize the leakage current flow between PV panel to the utility grid and minimizes the component count. Inside this article, modeling and control of proposed SPSSPVS are described. The control of the system ensures the maximum photovoltaic power harvesting (MPPH) and synchronization with the utility grid. The MPPH operation is obtained using perturb and observe (P&O), however for the synchronization of HBVSC a modified third order sinusoidal integrator (mTOSSI) based band pass filter (BPF) is developed. The mTOSSI extracts the synchronization signal even if grid voltage is polluted. The performance is evaluated using the MATLAB 2022a platform.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Control of High Gain Quasi-Z-Source Step-up DC-DC boost Converter for Standalone System based on Photovoltaic Pannels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: In this paper, a stability analysis and control design for high gain quasi-Z-source boost DC-DC converter (QZSBC) for standalone solar panels, is presented. To maintain system operation stable and supply the connected DC load at all times and in the presence of all conditions, the QZSCBC configuration is reinforced by a battery storage element (BSE). For efficient operation of the QZSCBC is controlled using the Perturbation and observation technique. Small-signal stability analysis furthermore, small signals QZSCBC is detailed. The developed control technique is tested by analyzing the small signal proprieties. The performance of the developed configuration of QZSCBC and its control strategy as-is tested using MATLAB Simulink.

Author Keywords: Quasi Z-source step-up DC-DC boost converter

articleTitle: Method of Mitigating Heat generated by rotor of a 45kW-Class Magnetic Geared-Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Subways are the most common transportation in South Korea, but they are very expensive to build and maintain and lack door-to-door connectivity, so trams are being proposed to compensate. Problems with the tram's drive system are more likely to lead to operation impediments, which can have a significant impact on traffic flow on existing roads. Therefore, it is proposed a new drive system, Magnetic Geared Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor(MG-PMSM), magnetic gears and electric motors form a single system which don't have a direct contact with each other so wouldn't cause operation impediments. However, after manufacturing a 45kW-class MG-PMSM, it was found that a large amount of heat was generated during the no-load test from outer rotor(Pole-pieces). It has been concluded that the heat was caused by poor insulation of the bolts inserted to join the pole-pieces during the stacking process. Therefore, this paper aims to explain the discrepancy between the analytical and experimental values and suggests where and how to improve the insulation to prevent such occurrences

articleTitle: On the Design of Simultaneous Motion Controller for the Four-axis SCARA System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper conducted the design and implementation of a four-axis Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm (SCARA) motion controller. Combining the SoC and FPGA circuits, a SoC/FPGA based four-axis simultaneous motion controller is proposed. The SoC-based controller operates the real-time forward and inverse kinematics computing, while the FPGA-based controller paralleled modulates the position and speed control of each axis. The SoC communicates with the PC-based host controller through TCP/Modbus so that the latter no longer requires the forward and inverse kinematics computing, in which the distributed control between SoC and PC can be achieved. The PC-based host controller only instructs the motion path order in the space, accurate path planning on each axis of the SCARA would be completed through proper movement segment calculation by the SoC-based controller, such design architect is able to accomplish a high speed, high accuracy motion control of the SCARA system.

articleTitle: Robust MPC with Integral Super-Twisting for Trajectory Tracking of an Exoskeleton Robot Arm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This work aims to enhance the robustness and reduce the control effort in the presence of input and state constraints while performing rehabilitation exercises with uncertainty in the model. To that end, a model predictive control (MPC) approach with an integral super-twisting algorithm for trajectory tracking is presented. The proposed method considers the uncertainties and disturbances due to the wearer-exoskeleton interactions while optimally exploiting the robot’s physical capabilities. Simulation and real-time results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional MPC and STA control methods regarding tracking accuracy and control effort reduction. As a result, the proposed approach can be applied to other wearable exoskeletons, providing a safe control solution for improving human motor skills in rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Efficient and Accurate Modeling of Resonant Converter for Real-Time Simulation Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient and accurate modeling method for the real-time or accelerated simulation of resonant converters. The method, first, derives a universal equivalent circuit for each switching bridge based on the switching function method. Afterward, an algorithm is proposed to find exact bridge status at each simulation time-point. The method can be used for i) accelerated simulation mode in CPU, and ii) to achieve a very small simulation time-step in the FPGA-based real-time simulation. The accuracy of the method is validated using a 200 kHz LLC resonant converter case against the reference model obtained from the Simscape Power Systems toolbox, for various operating modes. To further demonstrate the modularity and effectiveness of the method, a step-up cascaded medium voltage converter implemented with 10 LLC converters is considered in the accelerated simulation mode. It is shown that the proposed method is computationally efficient, reducing the simulation time by a factor of 19 for a system including four 10-LLC step-up assemblies, while rendering the same level of accuracy.

articleTitle: Investigation of Power Generation Reduction Patterns Due to Wind Speed Fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Conference on Power Electronics and Drive Systems (PEDS)
abstract: Currently, the introduction of renewable energy sources is being promoted to solve the problems of environmental pollution and global warming. In particular, the number of wind energy conversion systems installed has increased significantly in recent years. The introduction of conversion systems is expected to expand in the future. Wind power generation systems generally use Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control. However, MPPT control takes time to change the rotational speed due to the moment of inertia of the wind turbine. The output power decreases as the time to change of the rotational speed increases. Therefore, Deceleration Suppressing control as advantages over MPPT control. The Deceleration Suppressing control maintains a higher rotational speed. As a result, the deceleration suppressing control increases the amount of generated power by giving priority to high wind speeds for power conversion. However, it is not known, how high the rotational speed should be maintained. This paper examines the relationship between the factors of wind turbines and the average power reduction ratio in the numerical simulation.
